changes.evidence: Past group told on screen: in The Punisher S2 episode 9 ('The Dark Hearts of Men'), Pilgrim meets Kusack and Danny at their club; they call him by his old name Robert, recall him as a devoted member who vanished twelve years ago with their money, and Pilgrim says he turned his back on 'the Aryans' after the Schultzes found him in jail. Add the Aryan Brotherhood as a past group and add 'The Punisher S2' to left (he quit it before the series; he serves only the Schultzes after, an employer). The Punisher dialogue says 'the Aryans'; 'Aryan Brotherhood' is the name said on screen for this gang in Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D.

Past group told on screen: in Daredevil: Born Again S1 episode 6 ('Excessive Force'), Fisk reads out North's record ('Born and raised in Chicago, top of your class in the Academy... Yet here you are in New York') and North tells how his captain there punished his use of excessive force on a drug dealer, before he moved to the NYPD. Add his earlier service in the Chicago police as a past stage (name as described on screen; Fandom names it the Chicago Police Department).

The left title 'Daredevil: Born Again S2' is not a departure: in S2 episode 8, Buck takes Bullseye's (Dex's) bullet shielding Fisk and is carried into the locked courthouse with Fisk; his fate is left unclear. Being shot (or dying) is not leaving, he never quits or turns, and Fisk's Empire is not ended on Fisk's own record. Remove 'Daredevil: Born Again S2' from left.

Past group told on screen: in Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. S2 episode 8 ('The Things We Bury'), Bobbi Morse profiles the captured Bakshi: grew up on London's streets, 'military straightened him out till they sensed something off and washed him out', then a private intelligence contractor before HYDRA. Add his British military service as a past stage (the screen says only 'military'; 'British Army' is the dataset's existing name for Britain's military, used for Hunter and Buck Cashman).

Undercover service missing: in Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. S3 episode 8 ('Many Heads, One Tale'), Giyera, Malick's HYDRA man, works inside the ATCU alongside Luther Banks at Endotex Labs, guarding HYDRA's secret hand in the ATCU; in S3 episode 16 ('Paradise Lost') Coulson says 'Before the ATCU, Giyera spent years in Special Ops'. Add the ATCU as an undercover stage inside his HYDRA service.

Past group told on screen: in Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. S3 episode 16 ('Paradise Lost'), Lincoln says Gordon brought James into Afterlife and Jiaying caught him breaking into her private archives (stealing the Kree beacon) and banished him; James says he always knew Jiaying would send someone for him. Add Afterlife as a past stage and add 'Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. S3' to left (banished). His S3 service to Hive is raised separately as an owner call.

Past group shown on screen: in Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. S4 episode 14 ('The Man Behind the Shield'), flashbacks show the young Ivanov in the Russian SVR unit that tries to seize the 0-8-4 Coulson and May take; he says his SVR unit was tortured and executed for failing, and Daisy says she traced 'SVR detention centers connected to the unit number'. Add the SVR as a past stage before the Watchdogs.

owner_calls.question: In Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. S3 episodes 18-22, James serves Hive under Hive's mind control (he distracts S.H.I.E.L.D. so Daisy can kidnap Radcliffe in Romania, then helps launch the warhead with Giyera). Forced/possessed service counts, but the screen never names Hive's following. Should this be a stage, and under what name?
options: Add a 'HYDRA' stage in S3 (Hive's and Giyera's own records file Hive's following as HYDRA; Hive bought Union City with HYDRA money)
Add a stage under a new owner-chosen name for Hive's Inhumans
owner_calls.evidence: S3 episode 18 'The Singularity': under Hive's orders James travels to Romania to help kidnap Holden Radcliffe; S3 episode 22 'Ascension': Hellfire and Giyera fly Zephyr One for Hive. In S4 episode 4 he says he never wanted Hive's mind control. The same question covers Holden Radcliffe (T:st-holden-radcliffe), kidnapped in S3 episode 18 and then working for Hive to create Primitives (forced service vs captive).

owner_calls.question: In Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. S2 episodes 21-22, Cal (not an Inhuman) carries out Jiaying's Afterlife war on S.H.I.E.L.D.: he lets himself be taken aboard the Iliad as part of her plan and says he means to kill as many agents as he can, then turns on her and kills her. Does this count as service in Afterlife (a stage, then a turn-and-leave in S2), or is he only her ally?
options: Add 'Afterlife' as an S2 stage after the Slicing Talons, then the existing Independent/left S2
Leave as is (husband and ally, not a member)
owner_calls.evidence: S2 episode 21 'S.O.S. Part One': Cal tells Coulson he took his formula of his own will to help Jiaying and is there 'to take out as many as I can'; S2 episode 22 'S.O.S. Part Two': Jiaying calls his siding with S.H.I.E.L.D. a betrayal of 'her people', and he kills her.
